findings.message: PlayGameUseCase's per-item rating key (itemKeyOf) used the bare symbolCharacter/thaiWord with no kind prefix. A Mix round draws from both pools at once, and a symbol character can coincide with a vocab word's exact Thai spelling (e.g. "ณ", a consonant that is also a one-character preposition) — rating both as separate items in the same round would collapse into one record in recordRating's de-dupe filter (`ratings.filter(r => r.itemKey !== itemKey)`), silently undercounting ratedCount/ratingCounts/accuracy in the finished summary and persisted history entry. This is a real cross-task alignment gap: task 2.1 introduced the word pool/kind, task 2.3 introduced the Mix pool combining both kinds in one round, and PlayGameUseCase's key derivation (built in an earlier phase) was never revisited for the new collision surface phase 2 opens up.
findings.recommendation: Prefix itemKeyOf's return value with item.kind (fixed as `${item.kind}:${...}`).

findings.message: Task 2.3's GamePage-level AC8 test ("fills a Mix round from both pools when one pool alone can't supply the requested count") used a fixture (10 symbols, 3 words) where the default item count (10) was already fully satisfiable by the script pool alone, and the assertion only checked that 10 screens were traversed — never that any word item was actually rendered. A bug that silently dropped WordGameItemSource from Mix's source list entirely would have produced the identical eligible-count text ("10") and the identical screensTraversed===10 outcome, so this test read as covering AC8 without actually being able to catch the failure it names. Task 2.1's own analogous test ("a deterministic mixed-pool draw contains at least one of each kind") got this right — a fixture sized so neither pool alone can satisfy the request, a mathematical (not statistical) guarantee — but that pattern wasn't carried up to the page-level proof task 2.3 added on top of it.
findings.recommendation: Shrink both pools below the requested item count (4 symbols, 4 words, itemCount 6 — mathematically forces >=2 of each kind) and assert both a symbol and a word were actually rendered during the round, not just that the round completed.

findings.message: Ten of this phase's criteria (task 2.2 AC2-AC5; task 2.3 AC2,AC3,AC5,AC7,AC8,AC9) carry no recorded red_proof — their tests have never been observed failing. I read each test by hand against its criterion and every one asserts the right thing (verified: WordProductionChallenge's no-autoplay/paper-mode/no-audio/RatingButtons-timing tests; GamePage's Mix-dispatch, empty-pool-blocking, history-pools-label, legacy-fallback, default-pool, and pool-selector-accessibility tests) — so this reads as an audit-trail gap rather than a masked functional defect, but it is still unproven per this plan's own red-proof discipline.
findings.why_not_fixed: producing ten independent red proofs is proof-generation work scoped to the executor's own per-criterion workflow (mutate, observe-red, revert, observe-green), not a code repair I can make in-line without re-running that whole loop for each test in a file I did not author the mutation history for.
findings.effort_basis: for each of the ten named tests: apply one small mutation to the guarded behavior, run `plan-runner macro run observe-red` against that locator to confirm the assertion fires, then revert and confirm green — bounded per-test but the callers/mutations differ enough per criterion (audio construction, radio-button dispatch, history rendering, pool-selector labeling) that it cannot be done as one batch operation.

findings.message: Task 2.1's own final structured-output call was rejected by the harness's schema validator ("must NOT have additional properties ('input' is not allowed)"), so the task never transitioned to task_status: complete despite the executor's own record showing all gates green (36/36 domain tests, build passing with only the three known out-of-scope errors) and every AC's test present and passing. As a direct consequence, the criteria ledger shows all eight of task 2.1's ACs as [none] (no ac_tests mapping at all) even though the tests genuinely exist, run, and pass — I verified this myself by running them. This is a runner/harness defect, not a code defect in the diff.
findings.why_not_fixed: per standing policy this is raised once as a named orchestration symptom for a human to fix outside the review loop, not a repair I make.

lessons.lesson: vitest tests may be run directly via `npx vitest run <path> -t <name>` even when `npm test -- <path>` is refused by the harness's whole-suite guard — useful for verifying a targeted fix without tripping the 'no whole-suite runs' rule.

A fixture sized so one pool already meets the default/requested item count (e.g. 10 symbols for a 10-item Mix round) lets a 'draws from both pools' assertion pass even if one source were silently dropped; size fixtures below the requested count on both sides to get a mathematical (not statistical) guarantee, as task 2.1's own domain-level test already models.
